system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Seller Package Review Against the Buyer Playbook

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package departs from our playbook on almost every material point. Several of its positions would move significant risk onto the Buyer, including a consent-on-delivery structure for Bluefen and a post-Completion Riverlark release. Its "key negotiated positions" and "fair and balanced" language does not make any of them agreed or cleared. Nothing in the package has passed our authority process, so we should treat all of it as the Seller's opening ask.

Two cautions before the detail:
- Our 20% / AUD 4.8m cap and 18-month period are conditional fallbacks that need Amelia Frost's written authority identifying the draft. None has been given, so we should not signal acceptance of either.
- The Seller's statements that consents are not legally required (DL 1.4, 7, 9) are assertions. We should neither accept nor dispute them until verified.

## 1. Liability architecture

| Issue | Seller position | Playbook | Pushback |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (cl 12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6m (fallback only with authority) | Reject. Hold 25% / AUD 6m. |
| De minimis (cl 12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Reject. |
| Basket (cl 12.2) | AUD 250,000, recoverable only above the basket | AUD 50,000, first-dollar once exceeded | Reject. The Seller's version is a deductible, which is a major change. |
| General time limit (cl 12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months (18 months is fallback only with authority) | Reject. Hold 24 months. |
| Time-limit override | Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise | Keep categories separate; no hidden general-regime override | Reject. This would sweep title, tax, IP and fraud into the general regime. |

**Why the basket matters:** Suppose four valid general claims of AUD 60,000 each (AUD 240,000 total).
- Under the Seller's terms, none is recoverable, because aggregate claims never exceed AUD 250,000.
- Under our terms, the AUD 50,000 basket is exceeded and the full AUD 240,000 is recoverable, subject to the cap.

This assumes each claim counts toward the basket. The playbook does not say how sub-de-minimis claims are treated, so that point should be settled explicitly in drafting.

## 2. Fundamental / Title and capacity

The Seller wants capacity and title warranties subject to the general caps and time limits "for administrative simplicity." This is the most serious structural departure. Our position is a separate Fundamental/Title regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. **Reject outright.** Fundamental warranties must not be folded into the general regime.

## 3. Fraud and exclusive remedy

Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature," and the Seller's text has no fraud carve-out. Our playbook requires fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct to be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this. **Reject, and insert the carve-out expressly.**

## 4. Disclosure and buyer knowledge

- **Disclosure (Schedule 7; DL 1.1, 1.2):** The Seller discloses the whole data room (to 5pm, 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public searchable records. Our playbook rejects whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure. **Reject. Accept specific fair disclosure only.**
- **Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3):** The Buyer has no claim for any matter it or its advisers knew of, including anything discoverable in the data room or public records. Our playbook requires deletion of blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier must name Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry, and must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity. **Delete cl 8.3.**

## 5. Material-contract and financing conditions

**Bluefen (cl 3/6.3; DL 2):** Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (~30%). The Seller offers reasonable endeavours and treats consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. The disclosure confirms no final consent and no evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are met.
- Our playbook requires effective consent **and** evidence that its conditions are satisfied before Completion. Consent-on-delivery is not acceptable, and reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- **Push back:** Make effective consent plus evidence of cl 11.3 compliance a condition precedent to Completion. Consider whether the Buyer needs a price or walk-away right if it is not obtained. That is a decision for Amelia Frost.

**Riverlark (cl 2/7; DL 3):** About AUD 3.2m is outstanding. The Seller offers a release "following Completion." The disclosure confirms the facility has not been repaid and no discharge is included.
- Our playbook requires a current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases. A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Push back:** Require a current payoff letter (the AUD 3.2m is "approximately" and must be refreshed), payment from Completion funds, and executed releases delivered at Completion.

## 6. Funds flow and employee bonuses

DL 5 and the funds flow note confirm the AUD 420,000 DD-005 bonuses are not in the draft funds flow. The Seller calls them "a matter for the Seller" but does not itemise them. Payroll tax and superannuation or on-costs are not addressed.
- Our playbook requires the bonuses (plus triggered on-costs) to be either a specific line item or Seller-funded, and the funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Push back:** Add a specific funds-flow line for the bonuses and triggered on-costs, or make them Seller-funded. Get an on-cost calculation. Clarify who bears amounts if the continued-employment conditions are not met.

## 7. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1; DL 4)

The Seller limits the indemnity to the SOW3 payment and calls it "adequate." DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer of SOW3 Project Materials conditional on payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open, which is not independent verification of non-payment. The data room has no receipt or confirmatory assignment.
- Our playbook requires a broadened indemnity that preserves the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180,000 must not be treated as verified either way.
- **Push back:** Broaden the indemnity to cover ownership and transfer of the Project Materials and related claims. Preserve the SOW3 cure. Request a payment receipt or confirmatory assignment. Do not accept "adequate" as a conclusion.

## 8. Export / privacy incident (cl 4.6, Sch 6; DL 6; DD-006)

The Seller calls this a "preliminary operational matter" that is "not expected to be material." The disclosure says a download link went to an unintended external address, the export may contain about 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps), and it is unknown whether anyone accessed the file or whether notification is required.
- Our playbook says to assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. We should not adopt "not material," and we should not assert breach.
- **Push back (process, not conclusions):** Require log preservation, a defined investigation scope, a notification assessment, and regular written updates before Completion. Whether to seek a specific indemnity for costs if notification is required is a decision for the principals. It is not a playbook-mandated position, so I have not assumed it.

## 9. Sandbar renewals (DL 8; DD-008/011)

The Seller calls the three AUD 110,000 renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) "ordinary-course operating costs." The disclosure says they must be read together for timing and scope, and does not say whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- Our playbook requires assessment, with no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Push back:** Do not accept "ordinary course" as fact. Assess whether the renewals are one arrangement, when they are payable, and whether they are terminable. Do not reclassify them as Debt or deduct from price automatically.

## 10. Tax, IP and Title

- **Tax/IP (Seller's summary):** The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime." Our playbook keeps them **open** and assumes no unlimited liability and no resolution. **Reject the "settled" characterisation.** Keep Tax and IP in separate categories, not the general regime.
- **Title (DD-012):** The Seller relies on the Company share register as evidence of title. Our playbook says DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- **Push back:** Require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. Examples are an ASIC company extract, a PPSR encumbrance search, and evidence of corporate authority. Those should support the Fundamental/Title warranty.

## 11. Office lease (DL 7) and Mossvale (DL 9)

The playbook does not address these. The Seller says the lease notification obligation does not require landlord consent to the share sale, and that the Mossvale assignment restriction does not require consent merely because shares are sold. These are assertions.
- **Push back:** Do not accept either characterisation without verifying the underlying clauses. Treat them as confirmation items for the diligence record, and confirm with counsel whether any notice or consent is needed.

---

## Summary of recommendations

**Priority 1 (reject and restructure):**
1. Bluefen: make effective consent and evidence of cl 11.3 compliance a pre-Completion condition. Reject consent-on-delivery and reasonable-endeavours-only.
2. Riverlark: require a current payoff, repayment from Completion funds, and releases at Completion. Reject a post-Completion release.
3. Fundamental/Title: separate regime, 100% cap, six years minimum, outside basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
4. Fraud carve-out: restore it from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, with no waiver.
5. Disclosure and buyer knowledge: delete whole-data-room and public-record disclosure and the blanket knowledge exclusion.

**Priority 2 (negotiate within our positions):**
6. Cap at 25% / AUD 6m (no concession without Amelia Frost's written authority).
7. De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000 first-dollar.
8. General claims period 24 months; no general-regime override.
9. Bonuses: itemise AUD 420,000 plus on-costs in the funds flow, or make them Seller-funded.
10. Ironquay: broaden the indemnity, keep the SOW3 cure, and get payment or assignment evidence.

**Priority 3 (information and process):**
11. Export/privacy: log preservation, investigation scope, notification assessment, and updates. Assume no confirmed breach either way.
12. Sandbar: assess the renewals. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
13. Tax and IP: keep open and in separate categories. Reject "settled."
14. Title: require independent evidence beyond DD-012.
15. Lease and Mossvale: verify the underlying clauses before accepting either position.

**Next steps:** Brief Amelia Frost on the Priority 1 items, particularly the Bluefen and Riverlark conditions. Any move toward the 20% cap, 18-month period, or any other fallback needs her written authority identifying the draft. Have NSW counsel review the mark-up, since I have only the Seller's summary and disclosure letter, not the full draft SPA, and the Seller's clause numbers may not match the final document.
=== END ADVICE ===
